rationale: The assistant opened poorly by assuming a drain fault and sending the customer straight to the pump filter without asking what was in the drum or whether water remained, but pivoted correctly on turn two to out-of-balance protection with a single heavy mat and ended with the right advice ('wash the mat... with a few towels to balance it'). It weakened fidelity by twice ignoring 'the full load yesterday spun fine', which already ruled out a motor/suspension fault, and kept pressing the same empty-spin check three times before conceding it was 'not strictly needed'. No fabrication, no parts, no unsafe instruction, and the conclusion matches the hidden truth.
